---
title: "Sliding Expiry (extend)"
slug: v/latest/cache/extend
---

`cache.extend(key, ttl)` keeps a cached value and makes it expire `ttl` from now. Use it when activity should keep an entry alive: a user is active, so keep their session for another 30 minutes.

```ts
import { cache } from "@warlock.js/cache";

// On every authenticated request
const stillThere = await cache.extend(`session.${sessionId}`, "30m");

if (!stillThere) {
  // the session expired (or never existed): ask the user to sign in again
}
```

It resolves to `true` when the entry was extended and `false` when the key is missing or already expired. It never creates a key and never changes the stored value.

## It resets the deadline, it does not add to it

`extend` sets the expiry to `ttl` **from the moment of the call**. It does not add `ttl` to the time the entry had left.

```ts
await cache.set("session.1", data, "10m"); // expires in 10 minutes
// ...6 minutes later, 4 minutes are left...
await cache.extend("session.1", "10m"); // now expires in 10 minutes, not 14
```

Calling it with a shorter `ttl` than the time left shortens the entry. If you only ever want to lengthen, compare first, or keep the `ttl` you pass at least as long as the original.

Laravel calls this `Cache::touch`.

## Accepted `ttl` values

The same forms `set` accepts:

| `ttl`                       | Result                                   |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `1800` (number)             | 1800 seconds from now                    |
| `"30m"`, `"2h"`, `"7d"`     | the duration from now                    |
| `Infinity` or `0`           | the entry never expires (expiry removed) |
| negative, `NaN`, bad string | throws `CacheConfigurationError`         |

## Works everywhere keys do

```ts
const tenant = cache.namespace("tenant.7");
await tenant.extend("session", "1h"); // extends "tenant.7.session"

const users = cache.tags(["users"]);
await users.extend("user.1", "10m"); // tags are left untouched
```

## Driver behaviour

| Driver                                         | How                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `redis`                                        | one atomic `PEXPIRE` (or `PERSIST` for no expiry); also moves the `swr` freshness marker |
| `pg`                                           | one atomic `UPDATE … RETURNING` on a live row                                            |
| `memory`, `memoryExtended`, `lru`, `mock`      | in place, synchronous, atomic within the process                                         |
| `file` and custom drivers on `BaseCacheDriver` | read the value and write it back with the new `ttl`, serialized per key in the process   |
| `null`                                         | always `false`                                                                           |

On `memoryExtended`, later reads slide the deadline by the new `ttl`, not the one the entry was written with.

:::note Sliding sessions
`extend` on every request costs one cheap command on Redis. If a request fires many times a second per session, extend at most once a minute (for example, only when less than half the time is left) to save round trips.
:::
